cookbook.ask: "Is my local cloud up, and what is in it?"
"Create a queue `orders`, send a test message and read it back."
"Make a table `users`, add three items and list the ones older than 21."

cookbook.it calls: skill `floci-triage`: `list_dead_letter_queues`, `inspect_dlq_messages`, `get_sqs_queue_attributes`, then `redrive_dlq` only after you say yes

cookbook.ask: "Compare my buckets and queues across AWS, Azure, GCP and OCI."
cookbook.it calls: skill `floci-multicloud`: `list_clouds` and each cloud's list tools

cookbook.ask: "Store a secret and encrypt a value with a new key."
"Start a local Redis and tell me the port."
cookbook.it calls: `list_marketplace_recipes`, `deploy_marketplace_app`; or with no extra tools, `call_write(cloud="recipes", operation="DeployRecipe")`

cookbook.ask: "Write the Terraform for what I have running."

troubleshooting.you see: `Could not connect to the endpoint URL: "http://localhost:4566/"`
troubleshooting.why: Floci core is not running, or `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL` points elsewhere
troubleshooting.do: Start Floci; call `list_clouds` to see what answers

troubleshooting.you see: `Cannot reach the gcp runtime at http://localhost:4588: All connection attempts failed` (or `azure`, `oci`)
troubleshooting.do: Start it, for example with the `multicloud` profile of the Floci UI compose file

troubleshooting.you see: `The aws CLI is not on PATH. Install it from https://aws.amazon.com/cli/`
troubleshooting.why: `run_local_aws_cmd`, the Glue catalog and Lambda deployment shell out to `aws`
troubleshooting.do: Install the CLI, or use the Docker image, which includes it

troubleshooting.you see: An installation ends `FAILED` with `'docker' was not found on PATH`
troubleshooting.do: Install Docker with Compose, or mount the socket into the image

troubleshooting.you see: The tool you want is not in the list
`Toolset 'x' is not allowed to be enabled at runtime`

troubleshooting.why: A typo in the toolset list
troubleshooting.do: The message lists the valid names

troubleshooting.why: More than one statement in a call

troubleshooting.you see: The first Athena query takes several seconds
troubleshooting.why: Floci starts its DuckDB container on first use

troubleshooting.you see: From Docker on Linux the emulators are unreachable

tools.description: Returns what an operation does, its parameters (required ones marked), what it returns, and whether it reads or writes. Read this before calling an operation you have not used.

tools.name: call_read
tools.description: Calls an operation that only reads. Refuses anything that would change state.

tools.name: call_write
tools.description: Calls an operation that creates, changes, sends or deletes. Same arguments as call_read.

tools.name: code_read
tools.description: Reads from AWS, Azure, GCP and OCI by running Python. Refuses any call that changes state. Runs Python 3 (standard library only) with three helpers: aws(service, operation, **params)   e.g. aws("s3", "ListBuckets"), aws("sqs", "GetQueueUrl", QueueName="orders") call(cloud, service, operation, **params)   catalogued Azure, GCP and OCI routes rest(cloud, method, path, query=None, json=None, body=None, headers=None)   any route of azure, gcp or oci Each returns the decoded response (errors come back as {"error": ...}; CloudError is raised when a call is refused). Print what you need or set `result`; keep output small by filtering in code. Parameter names are the service model's (PascalCase for AWS). Imports are limited to json, re, math, datetime, collections, itertools, statistics, base64, textwrap, string, functools, decimal, time, uuid, hashlib.

tools.name: code_write
tools.description: Reads and changes AWS, Azure, GCP and OCI by running Python. Ask the user before anything destructive. Runs Python 3 (standard library only) with three helpers: aws(service, operation, **params)   e.g. aws("s3", "ListBuckets"), aws("sqs", "GetQueueUrl", QueueName="orders") call(cloud, service, operation, **params)   catalogued Azure, GCP and OCI routes rest(cloud, method, path, query=None, json=None, body=None, headers=None)   any route of azure, gcp or oci Each returns the decoded response (errors come back as {"error": ...}; CloudError is raised when a call is refused). Print what you need or set `result`; keep output small by filtering in code. Parameter names are the service model's (PascalCase for AWS). Imports are limited to json, re, math, datetime, collections, itertools, statistics, base64, textwrap, string, functools, decimal, time, uuid, hashlib.

recipes.name: Apache Airflow
recipes.description: An open-source workflow orchestration platform for authoring, scheduling and monitoring data pipelines as code. Define your DAGs in Python and track every run in the built-in web UI.

aws.service: Amazon MWAA (Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow)
aws.parity: Amazon MWAA runs the same Airflow engine — your DAG files, operators, hooks and connections work without modification.
aws.deploy: Create an MWAA environment, upload your DAG folder to the associated S3 bucket and configure the same Connections and Variables via the Airflow UI or Secrets Manager.

recipes.name: ClickHouse Analytics DB
recipes.description: Column-oriented OLAP database for real-time analytics over billions of rows. Blazing-fast aggregations, a SQL interface and a built-in web Play console. A local powerhouse for dashboards, logs and event analytics.

aws.service: Self-host on Amazon ECS/EKS (analytics alt: Amazon Redshift)
aws.parity: The exact same ClickHouse engine runs locally and in your ECS/Fargate task — identical SQL, table engines and wire protocol.
aws.deploy: Push the image to ECR and run it as an ECS service; attach an EBS/EFS volume for /var/lib/clickhouse.

variables.label: Password

recipes.name: DynamoDB Admin

skills.name: floci-explore
skills.description: Survey everything running in the local Floci environment (health, AWS services with resources, network topology, estimated cost) and report it as one scannable table. Use when the user asks what is running, what exists, or whether the local cloud is healthy.
skills.argumentHint: [service key to focus on, e.g. s3]

skills.name: floci-generic
skills.description: Operate any service of the local AWS, Azure, GCP and OCI runtimes, and the Docker recipes, through the few generic tools instead of one tool per operation. Use when a request names a service or operation that no dedicated tool covers, or when it chains several calls or needs a big result filtered first.
skills.argumentHint: [what you want to do, e.g. 'list the queues with messages in them']

skills.name: floci-iac
skills.description: Export the resources in the local emulator as Terraform or CDK, and check a Terraform or CDK project for drift against what is actually running. Use when the user wants infrastructure code from a working local stack, or asks whether code and emulator agree.

skills.name: floci-marketplace
skills.description: Browse the Docker recipe catalog and start, inspect or remove local stacks such as PostgreSQL, Redis, Kafka, Keycloak or Ollama. Use when the user wants a local database, broker or tool running next to the emulator.

skills.name: floci-multicloud
skills.description: Compare the same kinds of resources (object storage, queues and topics, secrets) across the local AWS, Azure, GCP and OCI runtimes in one table. Use when the user wants a cross-cloud inventory, or asks where something exists.

skills.name: floci-seed
skills.description: Fill a local DynamoDB table, S3 bucket or PostgreSQL database with synthetic Faker data for development. Use when the user wants test data, fixtures, or an empty local resource populated.

skills.name: floci-triage
skills.description: Diagnose failed messages in the local emulator. Finds dead-letter queues, inspects what is stuck and why, then redrives only after the user confirms. Use when messages are not arriving, a consumer keeps failing, or the user mentions a DLQ.
